title: Build the base script
summary: Turn the Beginner preset into the Intermediate one, then see how it scores on roads it has never seen.

steps.title: Start from Beginner
steps.body:
This lesson rebuilds the Intermediate preset from the Beginner one. Intermediate is the base every run starts from when it has no script, so once yours matches, you know exactly what a default run does.

The starter is the Beginner preset. First, give it the brain from lesson 3: `racing-standard`, with nine rays, the speed and the heading error.

check.message: The brain should have 11 inputs: nine rays, the speed and the heading error.

hints: The brain line picks the network and its inputs.
Change brain racing-starter to brain racing-standard.

steps.title: The lap bonus
steps.body:
Checkpoints are the dense reward that lets evolution see small progress. The lap bonus is a big, rare prize on top, so a car that keeps going all the way round beats one that only gets far.

Add `reward +10 when lap.completed` right after the checkpoint reward.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses lap.completed.

hints: Replace the comment with reward +10 when lap.completed.

steps.title: Speed first
steps.body:
Add the small speed reward from lesson 4, `reward +0.002 * car.speed`, as the very first reward.

Order matters here for a subtle reason. The app's built-in reward adds speed first, then checkpoints, then laps. Computers round every addition a tiny bit, so adding the same points in another order can differ in the last digit. Matching the order makes your script and a default run score every car identically.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses car.speed.

hints: It goes where the comment is, above the checkpoint reward.
Replace the comment with reward +0.002 * car.speed.

steps.title: Match the preset and compare
steps.body:
Two differences are left. Intermediate gives up on a stuck car after 3 seconds, which keeps generations short. It also has no `useTrack`, so it trains on whatever road you pick when you create the run.

Press Check to see the first difference. When your script matches, the check passes.

Then train it for 50 generations and open the Bench tab. The benchmark drives your best brain on five roads it has never seen and scores it from 0 to 100, next to the Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced reference scripts.

check.message: Your script should do exactly what the Intermediate preset does.

hints: Look at the stalled rule and at the end of the generation block.
Change 5 s to 3 s in the stalled rule, and delete the useTrack line and its comment.
